plain.text: Paul spoke to the crowd in Aramaic, and they became very quiet. He told them he was a Jew, born in Tarsus, brought up in Jerusalem and trained by the teacher Gamaliel. He had been zealous for God and persecuted followers of the Way to their death. On the road to Damascus, a bright light from heaven flashed around him and a voice said, "Saul! Saul! Why do you persecute me?" It was Jesus of Nazareth. Blinded, he was led into Damascus. Ananias, a devout man respected by the Jews, restored his sight and said, "The God of our ancestors has chosen you to know his will and to see the Righteous One. You will be his witness to all people. Get up, be baptised and wash your sins away, calling on his name." Later, while praying in the temple, Paul had a vision of the Lord telling him to leave Jerusalem, because they would not accept his testimony. "Go; I will send you far away to the Gentiles."

At the word "Gentiles", the crowd shouted, "Rid the earth of him! He's not fit to live!" The commander ordered Paul taken into the barracks and questioned under flogging. As they stretched him out, Paul asked the centurion, "Is it legal for you to flog a Roman citizen who hasn't even been found guilty?" The commander was alarmed, because he had put a Roman citizen in chains. He said he had paid a lot for his citizenship. Paul replied, "But I was born a citizen." The next day, wanting to find out exactly why Paul was accused, the commander released him and ordered the chief priests and council to assemble.

summary.bigIdea: Paul tells the crowd his story of meeting Jesus, and his Roman citizenship protects him from flogging.
points: Paul shares how he went from persecuting the Way to following Jesus.
The crowd turns violent when he mentions being sent to the Gentiles.
Paul's Roman citizenship saves him from being flogged.
summary.reflection: Paul's testimony was simply his story of meeting Jesus. What is your story so far?
